title: Stall analysis: token-surge and request-queueing investigation
summary: Standup notes and experiment log for an observed increase in tail latency and request queueing during token-surge traffic pattern on feb-21. Includes test matrix, raw numbers, hypotheses, commands used, and action items.
body:
Context:
- Observed a repeatable stall pattern during synthetic token-surge tests and a small number of customer reports (CS case #CS-2219). Symptoms: sudden jump in p95/p99 latency and visible backlog in request queueing leading to 5-10s stalls for some 1k-2k token requests.
- Affected surface: hosted-api and some Dedicated pools in region-us-west2; private deployments not yet reported.
- Hypothesis space: (A) KV cache thrashing when token-length distribution spikes, (B) batching scheduler mis-prioritizing long-running streams, (C) kernel selection fallback creating a CPU-bound path, (D) GPU-side PCIe DMA bursts causing momentary stalls.

Meeting notes (2025-02-21 triage, 10:00–10:45):
- Attendees: Maya, Diego, Priya, Samir, Jocelyn.
- Immediate ask from CS: create a reproducible test harness that simulates token-surge from many concurrent clients.
- Diego reported a kernel-compatibility warning logged on 2025-02-20 03:14 UTC on dedicated-prod-pool-a: "kernel_fallback=1 on model=redwood/open-7b-v2 seq_len=2048".
- Priya pointed out recent scheduler change (PR #3421) that alters batch-sizing heuristics for streaming endpoints.
- Agreed to parallelize investigation: infra (Samir) to capture sysmetrics and PCIe counters; runtime (Diego/Maya) to run microbenchmarks and instrument KV cache stats; product (Jocelyn) to collect customer traffic traces and map to config.

Repro harness and test plan (executed 2025-02-21 — logs below):
- Test rig: 40 concurrent clients, mix of: 70% short requests (<=64 tokens), 30% long requests (>=1500 tokens). Ramp to steady rate of 120 requests/s over 30s. Runs against: redwood/open-7b-v2 (fp16), redwood/open-7b-v2-q4 (q4), phi-2.8b-q4 (approx), models served from pool: dedicated-prod-pool-a (A100), hosted-usw2-general (T4).
- Commands used (summary):
  - run-loadgen --clients 40 --mix short:70,long:30 --rps 120 --duration 300 --model redwood/open-7b-v2 --pool dedicated-prod-pool-a --log /tmp/stall-test.log
  - sr-tool inspect-kv-cache --instance dedicated-prod-pool-a --model redwood/open-7b-v2 --after 2025-02-21T10:05Z
  - node-metrics dump --interval 1s --counters gpu_busy,gpu_mem_util,pcie_util,cpu_iowait > /tmp/sysdump.csv

Raw observations (single representative run):
- baseline (control run, even traffic): p50=42ms, p95=310ms, p99=620ms, max=1.8s, avg GPU utilization 68%.
- token-surge run: p50=45ms, p95=1.4s, p99=6.3s, max=12.4s, avg GPU utilization 81% (but with 3 spikes to ~98% correlated with stalls).
- queue_depth metric from runtime showed a jump from <10 requests queued to ~220 requests queued during spikes (sustained ~4–7s).
- KV cache miss-rate increased from 2.1% to 18% during token-surge; cache eviction rate spiked.
- PCIe util reported short bursts of near-saturation coincident with the backlog window.
- No obvious OOM; memory pressure on GPU did not cross threshold.

Hypotheses tested and results:
1) KV cache thrash is primary driver
   - Change: disable prefix caching on model for test run. Result: p95 improved by ~35%, p99 reduced from 6.3s to 2.1s, queue_depth peak reduced to ~90. Interpretation: caching logic likely exacerbates stalls when long sequences interleave with many short sequences.
2) Scheduler batch sizing regression (PR #3421)
   - Change: roll back PR #3421 on a canary node and re-run. Result: small improvement on p99 (~10%), but queue batches still grew during spikes.
3) Kernel fallback on specific sequence length path
   - Observed warning logs for kernel_fallback=1. Rebuilt kernels with additional logging and ran targeted microbench (seq_len 1536–2048). Result: kernel fallback activated for q4 quantized variant on a subset of shards leading to CPU-side soft-serial execution. Mitigation: pin kernel variant or force recompile path.
4) PCIe/DMA bursts as amplifier
   - Samir captured PCIe counters: short, high-amplitude DMA bursts aligned with KV cache flushes and long-token decoding. This seems to amplify latency but not primary cause.

Interim conclusion:
- Primary contributor: interaction between KV cache eviction/thrashing and scheduler heuristics under mixed-length traffic leading to sudden backlog. Kernel fallback and PCIe bursts amplify the effect but are not sole cause.

Quick fixes validated (2025-02-22):
- Conservative change to caching: increase per-session cache pinning ttl from 10s -> 45s for streaming endpoints. Effect: p95 decreased ~22% in 3 runs. Rollout PR: #3456 (runtime).
- Add a temporary batch-size ceiling for streaming queues under high variance. Implemented as feature flag: runtime.feature.batch_ceiling=enabled. Reduced max queue_depth by ~60%.

Longer-term work items:
- (Perf-4823) Revisit caching eviction policy to be workload-aware (owner: Diego, due: 2025-03-14).
- Kernel: ensure quantized kernel fallback coverage and automated post-compile smoke tests on seq_len 512/1024/1536/2048 (owner: Priya, due: 2025-03-07).
- Scheduler: adaptive priority heuristic to avoid starving short requests when long streams are present (owner: Maya and Samir, due: 2025-03-21).
- Observability: surface per-session KV cache hit/miss and batch composition in Console dashboard (owner: Jocelyn, due: 2025-03-10).

Action items (owners + due):
- Diego: open RFC for cache eviction algorithm (Perf-4823) + link design doc (due 2025-03-07).
- Priya: prepare kernel test matrix and add to CI (PR target 2025-03-03).
- Samir: instrument PCIe/DMA counters in prod canary and add alert threshold for sustained bursts (due 2025-02-28).
- Maya: coordinate controlled rollout of cache-ttl change across Dedicated pools and run customer-impact tests (due 2025-02-26).
- Jocelyn: reach out to impacted customers for test windows and collect representative request traces (due 2025-02-24).

Open questions / blockers:
- Is the cache pinning TTL change safe for memory-constrained small-pool customers? Need a knob per-pool.
- We saw kernel_fallback on q4 variant shards but not consistently across all nodes — root cause for inconsistency unclear.
- Need product guidance: do we prioritize short-request latency (PLG UX) or throughput for long-running batch inference?

Notes for follow-ups:
- Attach: /tmp/stall-test.log (raw), /tmp/sysdump.csv (sysmetrics), flamegraphs archived at s3://redwood-perf/stall-analysis/feb21/
- Next sync scheduled: 2025-02-24 09:30 (standup + results after cache-ttl canary).

One-line TL;DR: Token-length variance + cache eviction path -> sudden KV miss storms -> scheduler batches long requests -> queue grows; quick fixes (cache-ttl + batch ceiling) reduce the stalls, deeper work required on eviction policy and kernel fallback coverage.

Thread snippets / references:
- Slack: #perf-alerts thread id: C03PAF2JX (see thread starting 2025-02-20 02:10 UTC)
- GitHub: review runtime PR #3456 (cache-ttl change) and revert PR #3421 for canary trial.

Appendix: sample log excerpt (redacted)
[2025-02-21T10:14:07Z] WARN kernel_fallback=1 model=redwood/open-7b-v2 shard=3 seq_len=1536
[2025-02-21T10:14:09Z] INFO kv_cache: miss=0.10 evict=27 session_id=sess-8b3f
[2025-02-21T10:14:10Z] METRIC queue_depth=198 p99=6.3s gpu_busy=98% pcie_util=0.93

End of notes.
